description:
The profiles reference describes profile publication and recovery as a redo record applied forward, and the bridge README points at the same contract.

## Background

The reference carries the canonical adopter contract for profile publication: a typed durable journal, an external bootstrap control directory under a named protocol version, a transactions subdirectory under the data root, a verified sibling staging directory, mandatory recovery at every profile command, and rollback of a prepared transaction. Several other passages describe a profile application as one recoverable transaction.

Profile application publishes through the same record as every other mutation, over data-root and worktree paths, so the section states the shared mechanism. The bridge README points readers at this page for the recoverable-publication contract and asserts that the bridge maintains no second transaction model, so it moves with the page it cites.

## Success Criteria

- [hard] REQ-01: The publication section describes one synced redo record carrying the profile's written files, its removed files, and its event append, applied at session open.
- [hard] REQ-02: The page carries no description of a typed durable journal, an external bootstrap control directory, a protocol version, a verified sibling staging directory, or prepared-transaction rollback.
- [hard] REQ-03: Passages calling a profile application one recoverable transaction state the record.
- [hard] REQ-04: The page states that a profile's worktree targets publish in the same record as its data-root targets.
- [hard] REQ-05: The bridge README describes the publication contract it points at in the same terms as this page.
- [hard] REQ-06: The event catalogue's profile-lifecycle entry names the redo record as the commit point the operation reaches, and the generated events reference is regenerated from it.
- [hard] REQ-07: The page's cross-references resolve, and it restates no fact the storage reference owns.
title: Profiles reference states the redo record
